reference.title: Marginal increase of sunitinib exposure by grapefruit juice

evidence.quote: Marginal increase of sunitinib exposure by grapefruit juice; Cancer Chemotherapy and Pharmacology (2010)

study_design: Within-patient, two-period clinical grapefruit juice–drug interaction study in eight cancer patients receiving steady-state sunitinib monotherapy during one 6-week treatment cycle. Serial pharmacokinetic sampling occurred first without prior grapefruit juice between days 14–20 and again on day 28 after grapefruit juice three times daily on days 25–27. A single oral midazolam dose was administered on both pharmacokinetic days as an intestinal CYP3A4 phenotypic probe.

unresolved_issues.message: A DOI and PMID for the study article are not reported in the supplied paper text.
The study reports possible sunitinib doses of 25, 37.5, or 50 mg once daily but does not report each patient's assigned dose.
Patient identifiers and patient-level demographics, diagnoses, doses, concentrations, and grapefruit juice lot assignments are not reported in the supplied text; individual records cannot be created.

Eligibility included metastatic renal cell carcinoma, gastrointestinal stromal tumor, or tumors with no remaining treatment options, but the diagnosis distribution among the eight enrolled patients is not reported.
A second lot of the same grapefruit juice brand was used for the last two patients because of the first lot's expiry date; the affected patient identities are not reported.

Line 53 labels 122.1 and 182.0 ng h/mL as occurring 'with and without GJ,' respectively, but also states that exposure increased after grapefruit juice; line 14 explicitly describes an increase from 122.1 to 182.0 ng h/mL. The records assign 122.1 to the condition without prior grapefruit juice and 182.0 to the condition after grapefruit juice while retaining this source inconsistency.

Figures 3–5 contain individual midazolam AUC values and measured sunitinib concentrations, but no digitized figure values or figure image source was supplied; patient-level points and concentration–time courses cannot be curated.

Sunitinib pharmacokinetic parameters, AUC, Cmax, half-life, Tmax, relative bioavailability, and interval effects are population-model estimates or values derived from estimated parameters, not direct observed summary measurements.

After three days of grapefruit juice coadministration, sunitinib had not reached a new steady state on the second pharmacokinetic day; the grapefruit juice effect was therefore evaluated using a compartmental population pharmacokinetic approach.
The active metabolite SU12662 was not quantified; only sunitinib was quantified in this study.
